propositions: Write operations use relation-scoped idempotency keys (target_id, relation), allowing one ordered pair to hold multiple different relations simultaneously (e.g., blocks and relates_to)

Remove operations are pair-scoped with no relation parameter, returning only the most-recent net-active link, causing permanent non-convergence when a pair holds two relations and one is deleted remotely
Guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one declines to unlink when the pair's net-active relation differs from the peer-deleted relation, but the decline repeats every pass without resolution

Direction-agnostic deduplication of outbound ADDs on (vendor_type, target_key) without relation key causes outbound re-adds to be skipped, preventing G4 suppression and allowing inbound removals to reach G5
Making removal relation-scoped by adding graph/_links.py::remove_dependency symmetric with add_dependency allows _inbound_unlink_one to remove exactly the mirrored relation and converge
CLI and library unlink must remain backward compatible: optional relation argument defaults to None, preserving existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior
